title: 1 in 4 South Korean High Schoolers Sleep Under 5 Hours
paragraphs: Getting just five hours of sleep might be OK for a night or two. But imagine sleeping that little almost every night.
For more than one in four high school students in South Korea, that's what a normal school week looks like.
A new report has found that 27% of high school students get less than five hours of sleep on weekdays, while six in ten get fewer than six hours.
The report, published by the National Youth Policy Institute, looked at survey answers from over 54,000 middle and high school students across the country.
Health experts recommend that teenagers aged 13 to 18 get eight to ten hours of sleep a night. But in South Korea, just 4% of high school students get at least eight hours on weekdays.
And more than 70% don't even go to bed until after 1 a.m.

The report also found that students start losing sleep when they enter high school. Average weekday sleep drops from 6.4 hours in the final year of middle school to 5.6 hours in the first year of high school — almost 50 minutes a night.
It's no surprise that many try to catch up on sleep on weekends. Across all the students surveyed, average sleep time increased from 6.3 hours on weekdays to 8.2 hours on weekends.
And getting so little sleep may be affecting their mental health.
Among students who sleep less than five hours, 33% reported feeling depressed and 58% reported high stress levels — nearly twice as many among those sleeping eight hours or more.
